blocks.orig: Climbing Kilimanjaro via the successful 8-day Lemosho Route
blocks.html: Summit Kilimanjaro on the successful 8-day Lemosho Route

blocks.orig: The Lemosho route is one of the most beautiful and unique routes to the summit. It starts on the western side of the mountain, is less crowded for a more secluded hiking experience, and famous for its breathtaking views throughout.
blocks.html: Among the routes to the summit, the Lemosho route stands out as one of the most scenic and distinctive. Starting on the mountain's western flank, it sees fewer climbers, so the trek feels more secluded, and it is known for spectacular views all the way.

blocks.orig: This route requires a decent level of fitness and is one of the more expensive ones. Also, it takes a bit longer which is actually a good thing: this gives you the possibility to acclimatize properly, which is also why it has the highest success rate.
blocks.html: You need a reasonable level of fitness for this route, and it is one of the pricier options. It also takes a little longer, which works in your favour: you get the time to acclimatise well, and that is the reason it has the highest success rate.

blocks.orig: So start preparing for the hike of your lifetime and for the picture you’ll be taking on the summit showing off your biggest smile 🙂
blocks.html: So get ready for the trek of a lifetime and for the summit photo in which you’ll be wearing your widest smile 🙂

blocks.orig: Your Tanzania Trip offers a unique service throughout the climb
blocks.html: Your Tanzania Trip gives you distinctive care for the entire climb

blocks.orig: Climbing Kilimanjaro is the ultimate challenge! Little details can make a world of difference, which is why with us, you climb with professional guides, porters, and a cook. They take care of you during your ascent via the Lemosho route, by checking your health twice a day and serving you delicious food. Sounds like a bit much? Not if you want to reach the top! Because we know that altitude sickness can creep up on you unnoticed and that proper nutrition* is essential to keep you going during a strenuous climb.
blocks.html: Climbing Kilimanjaro is the ultimate test! Small details can make a huge difference, so when you climb with us you are accompanied by professional guides, porters and a cook. On your way up the Lemosho route they look after you, checking your health twice a day and preparing tasty meals. Does that seem excessive? Not if reaching the summit is your goal! We know that altitude sickness can develop without you noticing, and that good nutrition* is vital to keep your energy up on a tough climb.

blocks.orig: *If you would like to see the menu, we can send it in advance.
blocks.html: *We are happy to send you the menu beforehand if you would like to see it.

blocks.orig: If you like advice on how to prepare yourself for climbing Kilimanjaro, you can always contact us or read our blog How to prepare for climbing Kilimanjaro?
blocks.html: For tips on getting ready to climb Kilimanjaro, feel free to get in touch with us or have a look at our blog How to prepare for climbing Kilimanjaro?

blocks.orig: When you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport our Your Tanzania Trip guide is there waiting for you. He then drops you off at your hotel, where you can relax from your flight.
blocks.html: On arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, your Your Tanzania Trip guide is already waiting. He takes you to your hotel so you can rest after the flight.

blocks.orig: Preparation for your climb: You meet your guide before the start of your climb, where he briefs you and offers advice on what to wear, what to pack, and other important tips to make your climb as comfortable as possible.
blocks.html: Getting ready for your climb: Before the climb starts you meet your guide for a briefing, with advice on clothing, packing and other useful tips to keep you as comfortable as possible on the mountain.

blocks.orig: Our guide meets you at your hotel in the morning to take you to Londorossi Gate, on the west side, where your unforgettable Kilimanjaro climb begins! After completing registration and the necessary ascent permit formalities, you head to the first camp on the route: Big Tree Camp. Be sure to bring your rain jacket, as you have to cross a part of rainforest. After lunch, enjoy an acclimatization hike to Shira 1 Camp, gaining 300 meters in elevation, before returning to Big Tree Camp for dinner.
blocks.html: In the morning our guide collects you from your hotel and drives you to Londorossi Gate on the west side, the starting point of your memorable Kilimanjaro climb! Once the registration and the required climbing permit formalities are done, you set off for the route's first camp: Big Tree Camp. Make sure your rain jacket is at hand, because part of the way leads through rainforest. After lunch you go on an acclimatisation walk to Shira 1 Camp, climbing 300 metres, and then return to Big Tree Camp for dinner.

blocks.orig: An early morning wake-up call, followed by breakfast, sets the stage for a gradual ascent to 3,505 meters, offering a breathtaking first view of the Shira Plateau and Kibo Volcano. The hike to Shira 1 high mountain camp is relatively easy, taking about 5-6 hours, which aids in the crucial acclimatization process, a key aspect of successful trekking. Upon reaching the camp, lunch is served, with the option to either rest in your tent or take a walk in the surrounding area.
blocks.html: After an early wake-up and breakfast, you climb gradually to 3,505 metres and get a stunning first look at the Shira Plateau and Kibo Volcano. The walk to the high mountain camp of Shira 1 is fairly easy and takes around 5-6 hours, which helps with acclimatisation, an essential part of a successful trek. Lunch is served when you reach camp, and afterwards you can rest in your tent or explore the area on foot.

blocks.orig: Today you trek from Shira 1 Camp to Shira 2 Camp. This walk is not difficult and you can enjoy the amazing landscapes and the unique flora of Kilimanjaro's surroundings as you climb higher. On a clear day, Shira 2 Camp is the perfect location to see Mount Meru (the fifth peak of Africa). After lunch, take an acclimatization walk to Lava Tower Camp (elevation gain of 200m) to increase the chances to summit and reduce the chances of altitude sickness.
blocks.html: Today's trek takes you from Shira 1 Camp to Shira 2 Camp. It is not a hard walk, and as you gain height you can take in the wonderful scenery and the distinctive plant life around Kilimanjaro. When the sky is clear, Shira 2 Camp is an ideal spot for views of Mount Meru (Africa's fifth peak). After lunch you take an acclimatisation walk towards Lava Tower Camp (200m higher), which improves your chances of reaching the summit and lowers the risk of altitude sickness.

blocks.orig: The Lemosho route joins the Machame route today. The hike leads from Shira Camp 2 to the beautiful Lava Tower at 4,630 m (15,190 ft). This part of the climb has many ascents and descents, but offers magnificent views along the way. It is a long hike and you may start to feel a bit uncomfortable because of the height. It is therefore important to find the right pace in order for your body to adjust to the altitude. After lunch, you descend to Barranco Camp at the foot of Barranco Wall.
blocks.html: Today the Lemosho route merges with the Machame route. From Shira Camp 2 you walk to the striking Lava Tower at 4,630 m (15,190 ft). This section goes up and down a lot, yet rewards you with superb views. It is a long day, and the altitude may start to make you feel a little unwell. That is why finding the right pace matters, so your body can get used to the height. After lunch you go down to Barranco Camp, at the base of Barranco Wall.

blocks.orig: After breakfast you depart from Barranco Camp to the Barranco Wall. For many people, this is their favorite part of the climb. Once at the top of the Barranco Wall, you have a spectacular view of the Kibo Volcano and Mount Meru.
blocks.html: Following breakfast you leave Barranco Camp and head for the Barranco Wall. Many climbers find this the best part of the whole trek. From the top of the Barranco Wall the views of the Kibo Volcano and Mount Meru are spectacular.

blocks.orig: Afterwards, a more difficult hike starts to reach Karanga Camp. This route has many ascents and descents, so keep the right pace. You have lunch at the camp and after a rest you can take an acclimatization hike in the direction of Barafu Camp.
blocks.html: Next comes a tougher walk to Karanga Camp. The trail climbs and drops repeatedly, so keep a steady pace. Lunch is at the camp, and after some rest you can go on an acclimatisation walk towards Barafu Camp.

blocks.orig: Today, you hike to Barafu Camp (once breakfast is done, of course!). This camp is the starting point for your ascent to Uhuru Peak - the top of Kilimanjaro! You arrive at the camp around lunch. Have a rest and after you regain your strength, take an acclimatization hike to Kosovo Summit Camp (4,870 m) and back. Enjoy breathtaking views of the surrounding peaks and experience the thrill of high-altitude camping as you prepare for the final push to the summit around midnight.
blocks.html: After breakfast (naturally!) you hike to Barafu Camp today. From this camp you set out for Uhuru Peak - the summit of Kilimanjaro! You reach camp at about lunchtime. Take a rest, and once you feel stronger, do an acclimatisation walk to Kosovo Summit Camp (4,870 m) and back. Take in the stunning views of the peaks around you and the excitement of camping at high altitude while you get ready for the final summit push at around midnight.

blocks.orig: The big day is finally here! Around midnight, the ascent from Barafu Camp to Uhuru Peak begins. The climb leads over good trails and the most challenging part is the high altitude. Once you reach the summit you can enjoy a beautiful sunrise, which is quite impressive at this height! After a quick celebration at the top (because, hey, you just conquered Kilimanjaro!), you start a slow descent to the scenic Millennium Camp.
blocks.html: At last, the big day has arrived! At around midnight you start climbing from Barafu Camp towards Uhuru Peak. The paths are good, and the hardest part is the high altitude. At the summit you can watch a beautiful sunrise, which is truly impressive at this height! After a short celebration on top (after all, you just conquered Kilimanjaro!), you begin a slow descent to the scenic Millennium Camp.

blocks.orig: The Millenium camp is located in a tropical rainforest. When you wake up today, you feel a sense of relief from the reduced altitude and satisfaction from reaching the summit. After breakfast, you take an easy walk to Mweka Gate, the exit of Kilimanjaro National Park.
blocks.html: The Millenium camp lies in a tropical rainforest. Waking up today, you feel relieved at the lower altitude and satisfied at having reached the summit. After breakfast, an easy walk brings you to Mweka Gate, where you leave Kilimanjaro National Park.

blocks.orig: Your driver then brings you back to the hotel for a well-deserved rest. Unforgettable memories, breathtaking views, and a true sense of accomplishment await and will stay forever with you!
blocks.html: Your driver then takes you back to the hotel, where you can rest after all your effort. Unforgettable memories, stunning views and a real feeling of achievement are yours to keep for the rest of your life!

blocks.orig: Sadly, this is the end of your holiday and the time to go home has arrived. Enjoy your last hours in Tanzania before our driver comes to pick you up and takes you to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your flight home. Still longing for more? It's also possible to add a few days of safari or a beach holiday to your Kilimanjaro adventure!
blocks.html: Unfortunately your holiday has come to an end and it is time to travel home. Make the most of your final hours in Tanzania until our driver collects you and brings you to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your flight back. Want more? You can also combine your Kilimanjaro adventure with a few days of safari or a beach holiday!
